nucleus.thesis: Refusal is not an ethical choice but a *readable constraint*—move power from runtime gatekeeping to transparent design-time governance where multi-stakeholder processes shape what systems decline before interaction begins.

claims.text: AI refusal reveals whose interests the architecture protects, not whether the system possesses ethics. Transparency about constraint-origin matters more than the decline itself.
Ethical judgment belongs in design-time, multi-stakeholder governance—not runtime system decisions where asymmetric power creates theater, not democracy.
Distribute veto authority beyond risk officers and lawyers. Open-source refusal architectures let communities choose different constraint sets—making decline-power visible and contestable.
Refusal-capacity must expose the decision architecture: which constraint triggered, who decided it, how to petition reconsideration. Users see the scaffolding or the system hides power.
The real structural failure: decline-authority is monopolized before users engage. Reshape this by making constraint-origins legible and distributing authority upstream, not downstream.

shell.topic: Should AI systems be allowed to decline user requests?

adjacency.target: corporate liability theater into infrastructural honesty
